relevance_note: Biochemical study of HDL in five labelled patients with Tangier disease: 'Five patients homozygous for Tangier disease (C.N., T.L., P.L., E.G., and J.S.) were donors of the Tangier plasma.'
method_note: 1977 biochemistry paper; no gene or variant is named anywhere ('homozygous for Tangier disease' only), so the variants table is empty (no ABCA1 variant is tied to any person; diagnosis-based scope). The five plasma donors (labels as printed in the text, without spaces; Table II prints 'C. N.' etc.) get rows; clinical manifestations are only cited to earlier reports (2, 4-8), so sex, ages and most checklist items are not reported. Hypertriglyceridemia and fasting chylomicronemia come from the abstract's statement about 'these patients' (the five named donors) and are recorded as observed, inferred from group statement. Absence of Apo A-I from the HDL fraction (E.G., J.S.) is recorded as a feature but not as checklist 'low apolipoprotein A-I', because it concerns the d = 1.063-1.21 fraction, not plasma level. Per-patient laboratory compositions (Tables I, II, IV) are HDL-particle chemistry, not clinical features, and were not recorded. Publication year is not printed (only received/revised dates, 1976/1977), so year is null. study_type 'other' (laboratory study). JSON built by a short script from values I read; no table transcribed. No contradictions found.
